subject.title: fix: forward response-frame meta to clients

question: Should OpenClaw accept optional top-level `res.meta` as an additive Gateway protocol v4 response-envelope field, or require versioning or a different metadata location before merge?
rationale: The patch fixes an existing dropped metadata channel, but protocol v4 currently uses strict response-frame validation and automation cannot choose the compatibility posture for strict generated clients.

options.title: Accept additive v4 metadata after rebase
options.body: Treat `res.meta` as an allowed additive v4 response-envelope field, rebase the branch onto current main, and land after normal checks pass.

options.title: Version or relocate the metadata
options.body: Require a protocol-version bump or a payload-level method-specific metadata shape before exposing new top-level response fields.

options.title: Pause this PR
options.body: Leave the fix unmerged until a Gateway protocol owner decides the response-envelope compatibility policy.

recommendation.title: Accept additive v4 metadata after rebase
recommendation.body: Treat `res.meta` as an allowed additive v4 response-envelope field, rebase the branch onto current main, and land after normal checks pass.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent Koc is the strongest current-line and recent protocol/generated-surface owner in the inspected history.
